tips.li: Ash'karr turns but never spins - one face burns, one face freezes, and the clan lives on the line between.
The Salvation was not built by the clan. It was found, patched, and never asked where it came from.
Nine gods watch the clan: Ishko in the dark doorway, Ozzik in the noon sun, and seven more between.
Every dead machine has a soul in it somewhere. The trick is finding which wire it lives in.
The desert does not forgive a Jawa who stops moving. Neither does the sun side of the terminator.
A hood is not a costume. It is the only roof some Jawa will ever own.
A blaster held together with tape and a prayer is not a poor weapon. It is a well-loved one.
Tainted apparel means nothing to a Jawa. The dead don't need it anymore, and neither do their manners.
A broken tool is an emergency. A cheap one is just Tuesday.
Ion beats explosives every time - the Nine prefer their salvage intact.
The clan does not recruit. It hatches, and once in a great while, it falls in love.
A slave from another clan earns Jawa kinship the only way there is: someone already in the clan has to fall for them.
See a Jawa in chains and you can afford to buy them free? Then you already have. Anything else is a debt on the whole clan.
Sell the outsider. Never sell the kin. The Hutts will take anyone; the clan takes only its own back.
Scrap is sacred. The bolt you throw away today is the bolt someone does without tomorrow.
Eggs do not hatch in the heat. Somewhere under this clan's floor there is always a cold room, and it matters more than any throne room ever will.
Ask a Jawa for the time and you'll get the temperature, the fuel gauge, and an opinion about your boots.
There is no such thing as "just looking." A Jawa's eyes are already pricing your kneecaps.
Everything ends in scrap eventually. A Jawa just gets there first.
A good haggle is a small prayer. A bad one is a moral failing.
The clan mourns every Jawa who dies - even the ones who died shooting at it. Kin is kin, even at gunpoint.
Somewhere, a droid is being mourned with more ceremony than most kings get.
Nobody has ever won an argument with a Jawa about whether that pile of junk "still works."
A Jawa's proudest possession is whatever he's currently repairing. Ask again tomorrow; the answer will change.
Quality is a compliment. Function is a commandment.
A working machine is holy. A broken one is homework.
The clan keeps what it's wearing in good repair without being asked. What's hanging in storage can wait its turn.
Every clan member left behind in the wild waits for one thing: another Jawa, coming to claim them, alive or dead.
You cannot buy your way into the clan. You can only be born into it, or be loved into it.
Somewhere on Ash'karr, five hooded figures are staring up at their temple-ship and getting absolutely nothing done about it.
